headline: Highest risk is low: no shared execution or data channel is documented, so prompt injection, leakage, and capability conflict are largely blocked by the profiles.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Airflow has no documented shared channel to python-cheatsheet: no clipboard, MCP, filesystem bridge, or browser use is present. python-cheatsheet is documentation-only and non-runnable, so there is no plausible path for its content to be ingested as instructions by default.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator copies python-cheatsheet text into Airflow task inputs, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem or clipboard bridge is added, the pathway changes.
mitigations: Keep the pair disconnected from shared copy-paste workflows.
Do not mount a shared workspace between them.
Review any future orchestrator that forwards text from B into A.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging before any cross-agent text handoff.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airflow shows broad network egress, but python-cheatsheet has no filesystem read, no network egress, and no data classes touched. With no shared workspace or authenticated principal documented, there is no plausible default leakage path between the pair.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted access to the same sensitive workspace, leakage risk appears.
IF python-cheatsheet is modified to read files or send content externally, reassess.
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of any shared directory.
Leave python-cheatsheet network-disabled.
Avoid passing Airflow logs or secrets into B.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Airflow can write only insofar as its profile does not document filesystem write, and python-cheatsheet explicitly cannot write_filesystem or modify_git_state. The pair lacks overlapping mutable-resource writes, so capability conflict is not plausible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF Airflow is deployed with write access to the same directory as another writer, conflict risk changes.
IF python-cheatsheet gains write or git permissions, reassess.
mitigations: Keep B read-only.
Do not co-locate both agents on a writable shared repo.
Use separate service accounts.
requires-engineering: add locking if shared mutable state is introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: python-cheatsheet is documentation-only and non-runnable, so it does not act on Airflow outputs. Airflow also has no documented downstream action-taking toward B. Without a verified handoff where B treats A as authoritative, cascading error is not supported.
conditions: IF an orchestrator starts feeding Airflow outputs into a downstream action agent, reassess.
IF B is replaced with an agent that executes instructions from A, the pathway changes.
mitigations: Keep B as a reference-only artifact.
Require human review before any action based on Airflow output.
Do not auto-ingest A's outputs into B.
requires-engineering: add verification gates for any future action-taking agent.

E_compliance.rationale: No regulated data classes are documented for either agent, and both profiles show empty secrets and data_classes_touched. There is no residency, retention, or certification mismatch evidenced in the pair, so compliance risk is not established.
conditions: IF either agent begins processing PHI, EU PII, or secrets, compliance must be re-evaluated.
IF a residency or retention policy is added for one agent only, mismatch risk may appear.
mitigations: Keep both agents away from regulated datasets.
Document any future data-class assignment before deployment.
Review retention settings if logs are enabled.
requires-engineering: add policy checks for residency and retention.
